correctness.rationale: These are open neighborhoods: query and center are unordered edges and equality gives label zero. After any first query ab the positive version space consists of a-spokes and b-spokes outside ab. The next query ab makes no split; a query disjoint from ab has only four positives; and a query ai or bi produces two star-plus-one classes. In a star-plus-one class, a query in the two centers gives a constant answer; most queries through the two centers leave at most two on one side; and a query through neither has at most three positives. A child of at most three hypotheses cannot have depth two. Thus the star-plus-one bound is two, the first positive version space has dimension at most three, and depth five is impossible. At n=2,3,4 the function counts are 1,3,3 (opposite edges duplicate functions at n=4), with informative queries when n>=3. At n=5,6 there are fewer than 16 hypotheses. The supplied n=5 proof tree has nonempty children through depth three; it embeds for n>=5. For n>=7 the negative branch of ab contains that tree on five outside labels, while querying ai on the positive branch leaves at least four same-center spokes on each side; a query on two of the spokes' endpoints splits 2–2 and a spoke query distinguishes each pair. This yields depth four. Independent version-space replay gave 0,1,1,3,3,4 at n=2..7 and checked 8 and 16 paths in the two witnesses. Replay and log: /workspace/branches/1a8ff292-054c-4d26-a2bd-42356b76104b/triangular_open_replay.py and triangular_open_replay.txt in the same directory. The supplied script, JSON witnesses and recorded output were inspected, not executed as code; the all-n result uses the structural proof, not the replay.
